title: Why Being a Viking Was Worse Than You Think

secondary_collectives.CREW: Adult plain-tunic Norse boatworkers with distinguishable muted gray, brown, olive garments; never clone Eirik/Bjorn. Main cast count remains five individual references.
secondary_collectives.LOCAL_DEFENDERS: Two adult English coastal locals, simple gray/brown tunics, round shields and spears; never Norse protagonist palette clones. No fight contact or gore.
secondary_collectives.ENSLAVED_HISTORICAL_ASIDE: Adult workers/captives in undyed garments with faces turned away, sober treatment; contextual aside not an invented sale by protagonist.
secondary_collectives.INFORMANT: Adult coastal local partially cropped at boat edge, simple undyed clothing; exact transaction fictional, no invented historical witness.

variant_gate: Daytime/weather/opposed views must be explicit derivatives of reviewed physical place master, then viewed and frozen before scenes use them.
visual_contract: Original 2D adults: pale round heads, black dot eyes, small expressive mouths, matte colors, clean ink outlines, mitten hands, readable modest period buildings; no logos, generated text, fantasy towers, horned helmets, duplicate weapon props, graphic gore.
narrative_time_policy: Seasonal illustrative arc, no narrated exact journey duration or universal Norse biography. First 24 scenes establish a daily routine with illustrative cutaways, then late-spring preparations, summer voyage, late-summer return, early-autumn harvest, winter duties.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You wanted to be a Viking. A ship, a sword, a terrifying reputation. Instead, it is barely light, your shoes are wet, and a sheep has escaped through the fence you repaired yesterday.
scenes.authored_action: Low view of wet leather shoes and the sheep slipping through one broken gate rail; Eirik reaches after it.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Broken gate is opening-frame callback; ordinary farm, no heroic weapon fantasy.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Your partner points at the broken fence, then the empty wood basket. Your first conquest of the morning will be firewood.
scenes.authored_action: Aslaug points from the broken gate to the empty basket; Eirik lifts the basket to fetch split wood.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Same gate/basket positions as 001; no written chore list.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Imagine you are Eirik, a free farmer on Norway's western coast around the year nine hundred and fifty. This is an imagined household, built around what archaeology tells us about Viking Age life.
scenes.authored_action: Medium portrait of Eirik at the farm entrance with a hand on the gatepost, clothing and humble dwelling establishing the protagonist.
scenes.continuity_requirements: First explicit identity shot; farm and Norwegian coastline remain credible.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You have land to work, relatives to rely on, and the opportunity to join a voyage. That does not make your life comfortable.
scenes.authored_action: Wide occupied farm view: Eirik checks a field edge while Aslaug sorts useful supplies near the house.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Socially free household, modest resources; no universal claim that every Norse household looks identical.

scenes.narration_excerpt: And one distinction matters. Norse society was not an entire population of full-time raiders. Farming, fishing, crafts, and trade supported it. Going on a Viking expedition was something some people did.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik hauls a simple fishing net up beside the landing, with baskets and repair gear visible.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Illustrates fishing rather than changing into permanent warrior; boat stays ashore in background.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You might spend a season overseas and the next repairing a roof. The rest involves keeping your household alive until the weather improves.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik holds a loose roof board beside the same dwelling and checks the roof seam.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Spring maintenance illustration; no ship or sword magically appears.

scenes.narration_excerpt: The National Museum of Denmark describes the typical Viking Age household as farming and raising animals, with food planned around the seasons. Your real enemy has an excellent annual schedule: winter.
scenes.authored_action: Aslaug arranges grain, preserved fish and milk vessel into their storage places.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Shows seasonal planning through real objects; no calendar or modern text.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Before we give you the ship, therefore, you get the farm. Because if you cannot feed yourself here, crossing the North Sea will not magically improve your qualifications as a living person.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik shoulders a bundle of farm supplies and looks toward the field rather than the distant sea.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Return firmly to work setup before indoor daily routine.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You wake inside a timber house, with sleeping spaces along the sides and a hearth at its heart. Fire gives warmth and light. Smoke is the less charming member of the household.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik sits up on the side sleeping bench as the same central hearth glows.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Hearth, benches, doorway, posts remain fixed; narrated wake is illustrative return to daily routine.

scenes.narration_excerpt: There is no neat little chimney quietly removing every inconvenience. Roof openings and ventilation help, but the hearth still shapes your indoor air. You get close for warmth, then move away coughing.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik leans toward warmth, then raises one hand near his mouth to cough at visible light smoke.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Roof smoke opening, no chimney; thin smoke not dense toxic spectacle.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Breakfast means something the household actually has: perhaps grain porridge, bread, or preserved fish. There can be dairy, meat, vegetables, and berries too. Viking food was varied; availability was the catch.
scenes.authored_action: Aslaug sets a porridge bowl and simple bread before seated Eirik, with a small preserved-fish dish.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Small ordinary meal, not a giant feast spread.

scenes.narration_excerpt: An impressive feast is possible. It is simply not guaranteed every time you sit down. Somebody grew, caught, processed, or exchanged everything in that bowl.
scenes.authored_action: Close shot: Eirik holds the grain porridge bowl, with grain bag and simple cooking tools behind.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Focus moves to food's labor origins, distinct action from bowl placement.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Your partner, Aslaug, checks the stored grain while you pull on a wool tunic. Clothing is valuable work. Spinning, weaving, cutting, and repairing take time that your fantasy outfit never mentioned.
scenes.authored_action: Aslaug opens a grain container while Eirik pulls a wool tunic down over his undershirt.
scenes.continuity_requirements: No nudity; main Eirik garment palette identical after dressing.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Surviving clothing evidence shows wool and linen, with differences in wealth and display. Yours is patched. Replacing the wardrobe whenever a sleeve tears is not a reasonable household policy.
scenes.authored_action: Aslaug stitches the worn tunic sleeve with a small needle, woven cloth beside her.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Patch location fixed on Eirik's garment; no sewing machine/spinning wheel.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You wrap yourself against the cold, fasten your cloak, and discover another problem. Leather shoes protect your feet, but a muddy yard remains a muddy yard. You are already carrying it indoors.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik fastens his cloak and places a muddy shoe on the entrance stone, mud visible on its sole.
scenes.continuity_requirements: One cloak brooch and normal shoes; no modern boot soles.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Outside, your animals need attention before your ambitions do. A cow that produces milk is also a cow that eats. Keeping livestock means arranging food for creatures that have never contributed silver.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik tips a fodder bundle into the cow's manger beside the modest livestock shelter.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Cow introduced at appropriate farm scale; winter feeding concept does not jump season.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You turn the soil and work the small fields. In this household, grain, grazing, and fishing all matter. The balance varies across Scandinavia; this coastal farm is not every Norse person's identical experience.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik works soil with an appropriate simple agricultural implement along the small field rows.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Work ground rather than stage a battle; the cow remains by shelter out of close frame.

scenes.narration_excerpt: The growing season is a deadline. Rain can help the crops, then ruin your plans. You cannot ask the weather to reconsider because your future voyage sounds important.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik looks from darkening clouds to the worked field while rain darkens the soil.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Explicit rain variant of FARM geometry; one coherent weather transition.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Hay must be cut and stored. During the colder months, animals cannot live on your inspirational speech. Every useful bundle you carry now is a small argument against disaster later.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik carries cut hay to the shelter and places it on an existing hay stack.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Time advances to haymaking before summer departure, no contradictory early spring ripe grain.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Aslaug carries out work of her own, managing supplies and textiles, alongside the household's other tasks. Women contributed substantial labor and responsibility. That does not mean Viking society offered modern equality.
scenes.authored_action: Aslaug uses a drop spindle beside the household's supplies, thread collecting visibly.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Textile labor rather than anachronistic wheel; competence, no modern equality slogan.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Everyone's place matters. The National Museum describes free people, powerful elites, and enslaved people. Those at the bottom could be bought and sold. Your freedom is an advantage, not the universal starting point.
scenes.authored_action: Bjorn seated nearer the central gathering place addresses standing Eirik, visualizing unequal wealth among free people.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Use plain fixed seating, not throne/crown; no invented rank labels or infographic text.

scenes.narration_excerpt: There is a darker foundation beneath some famous voyages: people were captured and traded. That is not adventurous treasure hunting. For those taken, somebody else's profit meant the destruction of their own freedom.
scenes.authored_action: Restrained illustrative view of two adult workers led away from a familiar-looking family group, faced away, distressed posture, no violence.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Explicit historical aside, not Eirik's personal slave sale. Adults in simple undyed tunics, not cloned main cast; no auction tags, prices, shackles glamour or gore.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You, meanwhile, have a more ordinary problem. A tool needs repair. Ironwork takes skill and resources, and the smith expects something in return. Your axe cannot be maintained by glaring at it.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik inspects a chipped small working axe on a stump and brings it toward an offscreen smith's work area.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Smith can stay outside crop; forge implements plain, repaired farm tool not huge battle axe.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You trade what you can spare, then bring the repaired tool home. It is a better investment than owning a shiny weapon while your fence collapses.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik returns carrying the repaired axe and replaces the loose fence rail.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Exactly same gate: now repaired, sheep kept inside; loose repaired rail change is explained.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Then Bjorn arrives with news of a summer voyage. He has access to a boat and a crew, and enough standing to put the expedition together. You have enthusiasm and extremely modest savings.
scenes.authored_action: Bjorn approaches Eirik beside the repaired gate and gestures toward the shore.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Bjorn identity consistent, richer muted clothing, sheathed sword optional but not waved.

scenes.narration_excerpt: He talks about opportunities overseas: trade, payment, perhaps plunder if circumstances favor it. Those activities existed together in the wider Viking world. A man carrying goods might also be carrying weapons.
scenes.authored_action: Bjorn lays a goods bundle on the household table and gestures toward the coast while Eirik listens.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Goods and possible armed voyage, no readable invented treasure map or ledger.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Your decision is not simply courage versus cowardice. If you leave, someone must do your work here. Aslaug looks at the remaining tasks. Suddenly the voyage has an extra passenger: guilt.
scenes.authored_action: Aslaug gestures from Eirik toward unfinished field work and the household stores.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Negotiation and visible responsibilities; no angry-wife stereotype or written to-do list.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You discuss household needs, crew expectations, and what you can contribute. This bargain is imagined. The underlying problem is real: boats, equipment, food, and labor require resources.
scenes.authored_action: The three compare a food bag, a rope coil and Eirik's small purse on the same table.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Imagined bargain; no universal pay schedule, exact coined currency totals or contract text.

scenes.narration_excerpt: At the local assembly, free men gather to discuss matters and disputes. Norse law was not just everyone swinging an axe until agreement happened. Assemblies provided a place for negotiation and judgment.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik arrives at the local outdoor gathering while neighbor stands with folded arms.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Norway local assembly; simple gathering place, not parliament building or Iceland tourist site.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Your neighbor raises a boundary complaint. You think his claim is ridiculous. He thinks your confidence is ridiculous. Other people listen, because land and reputation matter.
scenes.authored_action: Neighbor points accusingly toward a small boundary stone while Eirik responds with an open hand.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Boundary complaint symbolic object; nobody brandishes weapon in legal hearing.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You cannot simply announce that you are the main character. Family connections and influential support affect your position. A free farmer has a voice; that does not make him equal to the wealthiest man.
scenes.authored_action: Bjorn turns to address the others as Eirik lowers his hand and listens.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Same cast positions and stone, influence visible through attention not giant noble costume.

scenes.narration_excerpt: The issue is left for further discussion, and you return to preparations. You would prefer to solve one crisis at a time. Viking Age life has rejected that feature request.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik walks down to the landing with a simple food bundle and looks at the waiting vessel.
scenes.continuity_requirements: First movement after hearing, bundle carries forward to loading.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Down at the landing, the boat needs work. Planks, fastenings, and seams must hold. Ships were remarkable achievements of craftsmanship. Remarkable does not mean they maintained themselves while the crew practiced looking dangerous.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik crouches by a visible hull seam while Bjorn checks a fitting on the boat.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Same vessel every sea/shore view; clinker planks and wooden repair tools.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You check an oar and help with the sail. A large textile sail represents considerable labor. Aslaug's world of wool and careful hands has more to do with your expedition than the songs suggest.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik examines an oar while Aslaug checks a sail-cloth seam spread beside the boat.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Real wool/textile work; square sail exact palette/mast fixed, no spinning wheel.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Food and water must come aboard, along with goods, tools, and personal belongings. Space is limited. You quickly learn the difference between packing for adventure and packing for a boat that must actually float.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik lifts the food bundle into the boat as Bjorn points to limited cargo space.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Water containers, rope and cloth bundles fixed placement for ensuing SHIP views; no modern barrel fittings.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Now the weapons. You have a spear and a round shield. Bjorn's sword is much more impressive. The National Museum notes that swords were expensive, while axes and spears were more accessible.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik checks his spear and round shield beside Bjorn, whose one sheathed sword contrasts with ordinary gear.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Eirik no sword, no armor/horns; exactly one spear/one shield, same colors thereafter.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Your lack of a sword does not disqualify you from being Norse. It mainly disqualifies you from looking exactly like an expensive television character. Wealth has its own costume department.
scenes.authored_action: Closer view: Eirik looks at the expensive hilt on Bjorn's sheathed sword, then down at his own spear.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Not drawing multiple swords or swapping actor gear; modest visual reaction.

scenes.narration_excerpt: And the helmet with horns? Remove it from the picture. The museum's helmet evidence does not support that familiar battle costume. You are traveling bareheaded, with a hood available when the weather turns.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik folds his simple cloth hood into his bundle, bareheaded short red-brown hair visible.
scenes.continuity_requirements: No horned helmet even as comic prop; spare hood in bundle, no sudden metal helmet on Eirik.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Finally, you push off. Aslaug remains at the landing while your world narrows to wood, rope, water, and other men's elbows.
scenes.authored_action: Aslaug stands on the landing while Eirik and Bjorn push the same boat away.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Farewell and cargo established; Aslaug never appears on overseas SHIP/MARKET scenes.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Then the wind changes. Oars become work instead of decoration. You pull, recover, and pull again. The man beside you is doing the same, so complaining does not make you particularly interesting.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik pulls one oar in unison with controlled secondary crew; Bjorn watches forward.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Sail furled for rowing, mast and benches fixed; oars connected and correct direction.

scenes.narration_excerpt: When the sail takes over, you still have jobs. Handling the vessel, watching conditions, managing equipment, and keeping things in order demand attention. Nobody has employed you as a full-time horizon admirer.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik handles a line with the square sail now set, Bjorn at side steering oar.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Explicit sail state change; no modern helm wheel/compass, no floating disconnected rope.

scenes.narration_excerpt: The ship is open to the weather. Your blanket is not a private cabin. Rain lands on your clothes, your belongings, and your mood. Dry comfort becomes something you remember with surprising affection.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik pulls his cloth hood up as rain wets the open deck and secured bundles.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Weather becomes overcast/rain on established SHIP geometry; same square sail reduced if needed.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You follow coasts when practical, stop where conditions allow, and depend on experienced navigation. Crossing open water remains serious work. Our imagined crew is heading toward England, not visiting three continents before supper.
scenes.authored_action: Bjorn watches a recognizable low headland while Eirik holds a line, coastline visible at a distance.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Navigation from coast/experience, no GPS/star chart/new continents or Norwegian cliff on English arrival.

scenes.narration_excerpt: On a rougher stretch, water comes aboard and you help bail. The sea has no opinion about your courage. It only requires the boat to remain seaworthy, whether you feel heroic or not.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik scoops water with a wooden bailer from low in the hull while Bjorn tends the steering oar.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Moderate choppy water, sail furled/reduced as explicit storm variant; not unrealistic breaking tidal wave.

scenes.narration_excerpt: At night, you try to rest in cramped conditions. Someone snores. Someone shifts an elbow into your ribs. You have crossed a vast body of water to discover that roommates are universal.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik curls under his blanket on one bench while a neighboring crewman's elbow crowds him.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Night after rain; cargo and benches same layout, no cozy cabin or beds added.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You eat from the supplies and drink carefully. Every extra day draws on what you brought. Weather delays can turn patience into a practical problem, even without a dramatic storm swallowing the ship.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik portions preserved food beside a water container while Bjorn keeps lookout.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Same supplies depleted slightly, no hot open flame aboard or feast.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Eventually you approach the English coast. Here, too, people know about Scandinavian travelers and settlements. You are entering an inhabited, politically complicated world, not an empty map labeled free treasure.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik and Bjorn look toward a low inhabited English coastal shore with modest timber buildings.
scenes.continuity_requirements: English geography replaces Norway deliberately; fixed MARKET_WATERFRONT geography established.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Bjorn listens to local information before deciding where to go. A poorly defended target might offer wealth. It might also be less poorly defended than the person describing it would like you to believe.
scenes.authored_action: Bjorn listens to a local adult informant at the boat's edge while Eirik checks shore cautiously.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Informant secondary face/costume distinct from main cast; boat moored near coast, no language text.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You land quietly away from the trading place and carry your shield inland with the crew. This is the portion people imagine first. Your stomach has suddenly remembered the portion where you could die.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik and Bjorn walk a grassy coastal track away from the waterfront, round shield and spear carried low.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Establish COUNTRY_EDGE camera variant derived from harbor district, no sudden Norway fjord.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Across a small open space, armed men appear. They are not waiting politely to become an anecdote. They have homes, allies, and weapons, and very little enthusiasm for your proposed business model.
scenes.authored_action: Across the same small clearing, two local armed adults step into view, Eirik halting at foreground edge.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Controlled adult LOCAL_DEFENDERS group in plain brown/gray, no cloned Viking capes; no contact/gore.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Bjorn considers the ground and the opposition. A retreat can preserve people and equipment. This crew chooses to withdraw rather than force an attack. There is no guaranteed victory hidden in your nationality.
scenes.authored_action: Bjorn signals withdrawal with one hand while Eirik turns back along the established path.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Same local opposition stays distant; no triumphant attack, weapon held safely down.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Back at the boat, an argument starts. One man calls the decision cautious. Another calls it humiliating. You call it excellent while privately checking that all your important body parts are still present.
scenes.authored_action: Back aboard, Bjorn addresses a dissatisfied crewman while Eirik checks his hand and intact shield.
scenes.continuity_requirements: English bay mooring, unchanged shield, no new battle injuries or bloody clothes.

scenes.narration_excerpt: That encounter is fictional, but the choice illustrates something basic: overseas profit depended on conditions. Not every expedition achieved a dramatic conquest. Failed opportunities still consumed food, time, and effort.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik checks the dwindling food bag and looks at an empty cargo corner.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Economic consequence of aborted opportunity, no claim of particular historical failed raid.

scenes.narration_excerpt: The crew changes its plan and approaches a place where exchange is possible. Weapons stay present, but the goods come out. You are now hoping a merchant likes your cargo more than your expression.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik lifts a trade bundle as Bjorn guides the boat toward the established landing near timber hamlet.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Arms remain aboard or held low; merchant dock geography remains coherent with 047.

scenes.narration_excerpt: The harbor has timber buildings, working people, and ordinary noise. Traders need information, contacts, and something others want. Being able to frighten a stranger is not the same as securing a good bargain.
scenes.authored_action: Wide quay view: merchant carries a bundle between modest timber stalls while Eirik approaches.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Civilian working market, a few controlled background adults, no giant towers/palaces.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You inspect cloth while the merchant inspects your goods. There are negotiations, misunderstandings, and the uncomfortable possibility that the other person understands the transaction considerably better than you do.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik examines folded cloth while merchant checks Eirik's trade goods on a small stall table.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Merchant ochre/brown fixed, table scale and bundles persist; no price labels or magic currency.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Silver is useful, but its form varies. Viking Age trade involved coins and silver valued by weight, including cut pieces. You watch a balance carefully. Confidence is not a substitute for the correct weight.
scenes.authored_action: Close view of merchant's balance with cut silver and small weights while Eirik watches.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Balance not modern digital scales; no invented exact numeric price, goods from previous scene stay.

scenes.narration_excerpt: The merchant adds a weight; Bjorn answers; the bargaining continues. Your imagined sale brings some silver and supplies. It does not finance a magnificent hall, a second ship, and retirement before your next birthday.
scenes.authored_action: Merchant adjusts one weight and Bjorn bargains; Eirik steadies the goods bundle beside them.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Negotiation action differs from inspecting scales; agreed small silver payment only.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Nearby, another traveler shows an object from far away. Viking networks reached extraordinary distances. That does not mean every farmer personally sailed the entire network. Goods could travel through many hands.
scenes.authored_action: Merchant shows a small foreign-looking glass bead to curious Eirik.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Merchant fulfills traveler-side illustration to avoid extra named actor; bead no fake written origin label.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You buy a small useful item to bring home. Not a mountain of jeweled treasure: something Aslaug can use and recognize as evidence that your absence produced more than interesting stories.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik exchanges small silver for a plain bronze brooch wrapped in a cloth scrap.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Gift fixed as bronze cloak brooch; no jewels/sword/crown, carry into return 067.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Before leaving, the crew repairs worn gear. Staying ashore costs time, but ignoring damage could cost much more. Even adventure requires maintenance appointments.
scenes.authored_action: At same quay edge, Eirik and Bjorn mend a worn rope section beside the moored boat.
scenes.continuity_requirements: One small maintenance job; hull/mast unchanged, no new ship or huge workshop.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Bjorn gathers everyone for the return. You check the water containers, secure the cargo, and look back at the harbor. You have earned something. Now you must keep it through another stretch of sea.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik secures the return cargo and checks water containers while Bjorn signals departure.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Silver/gift stowed inside small cloth pouch, no exposed jangling pile on deck.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Home is not one uninterrupted victory lap away. There are winds to judge and stops to make. You are tired of being damp, which unfortunately is not a useful navigation method.
scenes.authored_action: Bjorn judges cloud and coastline while Eirik tends a line beside the same mast.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Return at later summer before harvest; sea geography generic open water, no teleporting palace.

scenes.narration_excerpt: A cloak shifts in the wind and you pull it close. Sometimes discomfort is simply hours of being miserable while remaining very much alive.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik pulls his brown cloak closer against wind, shoulders hunched but alert.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Same damp wool, same cloak/brooch; not freezing through ice or inventing snowstorm.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You share work and supplies with the crew. The voyage depends on cooperation, including with people you would never voluntarily invite to dinner. Your survival has acquired a group project.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik passes a food portion to Bjorn while controlled crewwork continues behind.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Cooperation action, no weapon confrontation or duplicated main faces as background crew.

scenes.narration_excerpt: When Norway's coast comes into view, familiar land feels different. The fields did not suspend themselves during your adventure. Neither did the animals, the household, or the neighbor's deeply committed boundary complaint.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik recognizes the established Norwegian headland and points toward home landing.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Return deliberate geography and weather change; same SHORE master features from 039.

scenes.narration_excerpt: At the landing, Aslaug greets you, then looks at what you brought. You produce the useful gift. She produces a list of repairs. Both of you have been working; only one has sea stories.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik hands Aslaug the wrapped bronze brooch while she gestures toward roof and farm.
scenes.continuity_requirements: No written repair list because literacy not assumed; Aslaug same clothes, gift now in her hands.

scenes.narration_excerpt: The crew divides the proceeds according to its arrangement. We cannot supply a universal Viking pay table. Shares and relationships differed. In this household's imagined reckoning, your reward is welcome but modest.
scenes.authored_action: Bjorn hands Eirik a modest small silver share, crew bundles laid beside landing.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Imagined arrangement, no tally numerals or universal Viking pay ratios.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You set silver beside the expenses waiting at home. The tool, the roof, the supplies, the help you relied upon. Your triumphant return begins looking suspiciously like money arriving just before the bills.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik sets the small silver portion beside a worn tool and grain container, Aslaug evaluates.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Expenses shown as objects not modern bills, receipts or numbered running tab.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Then the harvest demands your attention. You work while the weather allows, gather what you can, and protect what must last. There is a deadline even if nobody writes it on a calendar.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik cuts ripe grain while Aslaug gathers sheaves along same field rows.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Explicit harvest-time advance, no still-green spring grain suddenly ripe within adjacent same-moment scene.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Food is dried, smoked, or otherwise preserved as appropriate. Storage is part of survival, not merely housekeeping. A meal you cannot keep until later cannot help you through the part of the year with less food.
scenes.authored_action: Aslaug hangs preserved fish and checks a covered food vessel in the storage corner.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Indoor smoke minimal; food-processing new action, fixed shelves containers.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Aslaug checks containers while you stack firewood. The household prepares for shorter days. A good store is reassuring. It is also a reminder that nearly everything here can be used up.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik stacks split wood under cover while Aslaug carries a covered storage container toward the door.
scenes.continuity_requirements: House/outbuildings fixed; declining light explicit, no unexplained giant wood pile added.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Your animals must be fed and sheltered. Keeping them alive protects future milk, breeding, and work. Winter is not just you feeling cold; it is the whole household consuming its earlier decisions.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik feeds hay to the same cow inside the open shelter as light frost covers the ground.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Winter timejump explicit, animal position and shelter remain; no deep blizzard for drama.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Indoors, a tear in your tunic gets repaired. Outside, wind finds another weak spot in the house. The season has a talent for testing every job you vaguely remember meaning to finish.
scenes.authored_action: Aslaug repairs a small tear at Eirik's tunic sleeve while he notices damp near the doorway.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Existing garment patch preserved; repair a separate seam/tear, no automatic brand-new clothing.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You mend the roof before the problem grows. Keeping rain out of the sleeping space will improve your life more than a beautiful nickname.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik braces a roof board and secures its edge to keep rain outside.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Same humble roof geometry; no new chimney, tools same repaired farm axe if visible.

scenes.narration_excerpt: A sore tooth makes eating unpleasant. Archaeological remains show that Viking Age people faced dental problems and injuries. You have people who may help, but you do not have modern medicine waiting nearby.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik pauses over simple food and presses a hand to his cheek with dental discomfort.
scenes.continuity_requirements: No gore, no diagnosis diagram or invented medieval dentist pliers.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You should not picture every Norse person filthy, sick, and indifferent to appearance. Combs and other grooming objects survive. Caring about your hair, however, does not give you antibiotics or emergency dentistry.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik combs his short red-brown hair with a simple bone comb placed beside his cloak.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Comb real object, not modern brush; grooming distinct from tooth scene.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You sit near the hearth while Aslaug works wool. The evening offers conversation, repairs, and perhaps a game. Life has pleasures. A difficult existence is not necessarily an existence without affection or laughter.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik moves a plain gaming piece while Aslaug spins wool beside the hearth, both relaxed.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Small personal pleasures; no chess board, modern chess pieces, playing cards or giant feast.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Then your neighbor returns to the dispute. He thinks you moved a boundary marker. You think he has developed a remarkably flexible memory. This time you bring someone who remembers the earlier arrangement.
scenes.authored_action: Neighbor points at a farm-edge boundary stone as Eirik brings Bjorn to look at it.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Same neighbor dispute resumed, fixed farm edge object; witness chosen Bjorn to avoid sixth mainactor.

scenes.narration_excerpt: The matter reaches the local assembly again. You speak, the neighbor speaks, and other men weigh the claims. Evidence, witnesses, negotiation, and standing matter more here than a dramatic battle pose.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik gestures openly to his witness Bjorn while neighbor addresses the local group.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Assembly winter variant, no shields/spears deciding lawsuit; no invented written laws.

scenes.narration_excerpt: A compromise settles this imagined dispute. You dislike giving ground, but an escalating feud would cost far more. The ability to swing a weapon is less useful than keeping tomorrow reasonably predictable.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik and neighbor lower their hands in uneasy agreement beside the same stone.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Compromise not celebratory duel; explicit imagined resolution, unchanged actors.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Bjorn's influence helped bring people together, and you have obligations within that network. Leaders could cultivate followers through wealth and gifts. A generous patron is still someone whose wishes can matter a great deal.
scenes.authored_action: Bjorn offers a small shared bowl to Eirik while others look to him, subtle patron network.
scenes.continuity_requirements: No royal crown or throne; gifts/relationships shown without universal fixed military obligation.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You attend a gathering and listen while better-connected men speak. Power in this world is uneven. Being free gives you possibilities that an enslaved person lacks, but it does not make every door yours.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik stands at side and listens while Bjorn speaks to the gathering.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Unequal influence, same geometry, no invented castle hall or new rich king.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Back home, you look at the remaining grain. You are neither ruined nor rich. You survived a voyage, avoided a fight, made some trades, and returned to work that never actually ended.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik peers into partly depleted grain container while Aslaug secures its lid.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Storage quantities decrease sensibly, not empty catastrophe unsupported by narrative.

scenes.narration_excerpt: That is the disappointment hidden inside the Viking fantasy. Adventure might change your fortunes. It does not erase seasons, responsibilities, weather, or people with more power than you.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik places the small purse back beside his repaired tool and sits heavily on the bench.
scenes.continuity_requirements: No trophy, conclusion through concrete modest economic state rather than text poster.

scenes.narration_excerpt: The spectacular stories deserve attention, but so do the hands that made sails, raised animals, prepared food, and kept houses standing. Without those people, the famous ships would have gone nowhere.
scenes.authored_action: Close view of Aslaug's hands completing a cloth seam, food vessel and useful farmtool nearby.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Hands behind legend, loom/spindle work; no sudden all-location collage or autogenerated headings.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You finally lie down beside the hearth. Tomorrow brings another fence, another chore, another calculation. Your terrifying reputation will have to wait until you have finished keeping the household alive.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik lies down on the established sleeping bench, Aslaug extinguishes a small lamp while hearth remains warm.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Proper nighttime variant, no modern candle lantern if not in HOME master; quiet ending before callback.

scenes.narration_excerpt: So why was being a Viking worse than you think? Because the sword was optional, the glory was uncertain, and the work was unavoidable. Especially when that sheep has escaped again. This is Viking Chapters: the lives behind the legends.
scenes.authored_action: Eirik reaches after the same sheep squeezing through the once-repaired rail, exasperated shoulders.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Opening callback: repeated gate failure explicitly another escape; cold-weather palette, stable farm identity; leave narration brand line audible without parasitic generated text.
